::: {.page-lede}
I am an advanced analytics professional and Applied AI Research Fellow with experience spanning business intelligence, operational analytics, market research, data science, and AI evaluation.
:::

:::: {.about-layout}
::: {.about-narrative}
I built my professional foundation through analytics work at New Balance and Forrester Research and through consulting and operational roles across multiple industries. That experience taught me to begin with the decision that needs to be made, understand how the underlying process produces the data, and communicate results in a form people can use.

## Current Focus

My current work extends that foundation into NLP, retrieval-augmented generation, synthetic data, document intelligence, LLM evaluation, and AI infrastructure. I am particularly interested in evaluation design: defining appropriate comparisons, preserving run-level evidence, identifying failure modes, and separating promising results from claims the data cannot support.

I am completing an M.S. in Data Science & Analytics in May 2027. My broader academic background includes graduate study in management and undergraduate study in technology management.
:::

## How I Work

I approach analytics and applied AI as connected disciplines rather than separate tracks. The habits that improve business intelligence—clear definitions, reliable data, appropriate comparisons, and decision-focused communication—also make machine-learning and LLM systems more useful and trustworthy.

:::: {.principles-grid}
::: {.principle-card}
<p class="practice-number">01</p>

### Start with the decision

Define what needs to be learned or decided before choosing a tool, model, or metric.
:::

::: {.principle-card}
<p class="practice-number">02</p>

### Preserve the evidence

Build reproducible workflows that retain run-level results, assumptions, and limitations.
:::

::: {.principle-card}
<p class="practice-number">03</p>

### Communicate for action

Translate technical findings into conclusions that technical and non-technical audiences can use.
:::
::::

## Beyond the Work

Before moving fully into analytics and technology, I worked as a mountaineering and rock-climbing guide. That experience continues to shape how I think about preparation, uncertainty, risk, and decision-making in complex environments.
